name: StartCrashReporter(url, handlerPath, databasePath): crash annotations, COM init, WMI survey, crash database, uploads on, crashpad StartHandler (child process)
notes: Contract: docs/contracts/crash-reporter-start.md (approved 2026-10-11). Hooked (WinMainInfra_StartCrashReporter), enabled in-game. Ours keeps CoInitializeEx(nullptr, COINIT_MULTITHREADED) and, when that is non-negative, CoInitializeSecurity(nullptr, -1, nullptr, nullptr, DEFAULT, IMPERSONATE, nullptr, NONE, nullptr); drops the annotations, the WMI survey, the crash database and its settings, the child process, the pipe/event/thread and crashpad's exception filter, and any upload; returns false. Test WinMainInfra_StartCrashReporter: 64 combinations of eight results of each COM call, original (stopped at its first dropped effect) vs ours on the kept calls and arguments, plus the exact list of the original's dropped effects. 9 mutants killed (apartment flag, success test, security skipped or forced, impersonation, authentication level, authority count, result, double call).

name: SendAnalyticsEvent(steamIdLow, steamIdHigh): HTTPS POST of the launch event (WinINet)
notes: Contract: docs/contracts/analytics.md (approved 2026-10-11). Hooked (WinMainInfra_SendAnalyticsEvent), enabled in-game. Ours does nothing: no network, nothing read back (the body buffer at 0x10fe048 is wiped by the original after use; the two statics at 0x10fe448 and 0x10fe450 are write-only; 0xc2df67 is the only user of WinINet in the image). Test WinMainInfra_SendAnalyticsEvent: the blocked path (the original makes one InternetOpenA call, ours none, buffer and statics unchanged) for five Steam ids, and the original's sending path in three endings (zeroed buffer afterwards, statics written exactly in the endings that write them) against ours doing nothing. 1 mutant killed (a write to the buffer).

name: install the terminate and purecall handlers (set_terminate then _set_purecall_handler, both with 0xcac170)
notes: Contract: docs/contracts/terminate-handlers.md (approved 2026-10-11). Hooked (WinMainInfra_InstallHandlers), enabled in-game. Ours installs winmaininfra::ReportAndReturn through a CrtSeam: kImageCrt (hybrid host) writes the game CRT's purecall variable (RVA 0x10dfb80) and the calling thread's _terminate field (+0xc of the per-thread data found through the FLS index at 0x104f89c, with the thread's last error preserved); kOwnCrt (standalone) uses std::set_terminate and _set_purecall_handler. A thread without per-thread data keeps its terminate handler (the original would create the data); the purecall handler is set regardless. Test WinMainInfra_InstallHandlers: the CRT's FlsGetValue wrapper, GetLastError and SetLastError faked on both sides, twelve variants; compares the call log, both variables (as 'is the handler') and every other byte of the per-thread data; WinMainInfra_InstallHandlersSeams: order and the standalone seam. 9 mutants killed (order, offset, purecall RVA, last-error save and restore, -1 and out-of-index guards, wrong seam); 1 equivalent survivor (the two setters of kOwnCrt swapped: both get the same handler).

name: terminate/purecall handler: take the top-level exception filter, put it back, fault on address 0 under __try/__except(filter(info))
notes: Contract: docs/contracts/terminate-handlers.md. Not hooked: only the installer 0xcac1f0 refers to it, and ours installs winmaininfra::ReportAndReturn. Test WinMainInfra_ReportAndReturn: SetUnhandledExceptionFilter and UnhandledExceptionFilter faked on both sides (the CRT's SEH registration validator 0x829c90 redirected, as in tests/winmain_run_app.cpp); filter installed or not, answering handle or continue-search, three repeats; compares the call log (exception code, flags, parameter count, read/write kind, address) and whether the call returned or the exception reached the caller. 4 mutants killed (filter not put back, fallback filter, fault address, read dropped).

name: shared_vf_4dc940: mov byte [ecx+0x10], 0 (5 bytes, folded with unrelated classes)
notes: Never hooked (5 bytes, shared_vf). WinMain calls it on the memory-tracking object at 0x10fda2c when the memoryReport switch is absent; winmaininfra::WinMainBody does the store inline (clears the byte at +0x10), so it does not block WinMain. Tested as part of WinMainInfra_WinMain (the byte before and after, with and without the switch; mutants on the offset and the condition killed).
